himalayas::hm_nvidia_senior-software-eng.title: Senior Software Engineer - Autonomous Vehicles
himalayas::hm_nvidia_senior-software-eng.description:
Categories: Developer, Software Engineer, Autonomous Vehicle Software Engineer, Embedded Software Engineer, C# Software Engineer, GPU Software Engineer

Self-driving cars need to know where the road goes, in real time, with no prior map to lean on.

Self-driving cars need to know where the road goes, in real time, with no prior map to lean on. We’re building the perception-based world model stack that makes this possible. It takes raw multi-sensor input and produces a live, accurate 3D model of lanes, boundaries, crosswalks, intersection topology, and traffic control semantics. It also fuses perception, map, and localization data into a consistent model of the driving environment that the rest of the driving stack depends on. You will join a team of world-class software engineers improving these algorithms. This is a software engineering role: algorithms are only as good as the software that runs them, so we need an engineer who obsesses over quality, performance, and architecture, and who can turn algorithmic ideas into safe, fast, maintainable code for production vehicles on NVIDIA DRIVE Orin and Thor. Your code will meet ASIL-B/D requirements and ship across L2++, L3, and L4 programs. What you’ll be doing: Build and own core online world model and context fusion software that runs in the car, from architecture through implementation to deployment. Write production C++ for real-time embedded systems, with a focus on correctness, determinism, and maintainability. Design software architecture, interfaces, and data flows that promote code reuse and clean boundaries across vehicle programs, while meeting CPU, memory, and latency budgets. Profile complex pipelines, find bottlenecks, and deliver measurable improvements in CPU utilization, memory usage, and end-to-end latency, backed by reproducible measurements on Orin and Thor. Develop benchmarks and performance regression tests that track improvements and prevent regressions. Use GPU parallelism (CUDA) where it helps to accelerate compute-heavy mapping components. Implement and integrate algorithmic solutions from the mapping team into NVIDIA ’s AV stack, working closely with algorithm engineers to understand and refine them while preserving behavior, output quality, and correctness. Develop to automotive safety standards (ASIL-B/D): apply strong static analysis, follow safety-oriented coding guidelines, and achieve 100% line and branch coverage with rigorous unit and integration tests. Build software that is robust to the varied conditions and failure modes of vehicles operating around the world. Contribute to code reviews and uphold the team’s quality and safety expectations. What we need to see: PhD with 1+ year, MS with 3+ years, or BS with 5+ years of relevant experience in Computer Science, Electrical or Computer Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience. 5+ years of experience building robust, production-quality software 3+ years of professional modern C++ development, with a strong grasp of memory management, concurrency, and performance. Demonstrated ability to profile and optimize CPU utilization, memory consumption, and latency using profilers and benchmarks under representative workloads. Solid understanding of algorithms and data structures and their impact on performance. Experience designing software architecture and APIs for large, long-lived codebases. A quality-first, systematic approach to debugging and optimization: comfort with static analysis, unit testing, and high-coverage test strategies. VLSI Design Engineer

Job Title: VLSI Design Engineer
Location: United States (Remote)
Work Mode: 100% Remote
Experience: 2–8 Years
Salary Range: $95,000 – $165,000 per year
Employment Type: Full-Time

Job Summary

We are seeking a talented and experienced VLSI Design Engineer to join our semiconductor engineering team in the United States. The ideal candidate will be responsible for designing, developing, verifying, and optimizing digital integrated circuits (ICs), ASICs, and SoC architectures.

The candidate should have strong knowledge of RTL design, Verilog/SystemVerilog, digital logic design, and semiconductor design methodologies. This position offers a fully remote work opportunity for qualified candidates across the United States.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and develop digital circuits and RTL modules for ASIC and SoC platforms.

  • Write, review, and optimize RTL code using Verilog and SystemVerilog.

  • Perform RTL design, simulation, synthesis, and functional verification.

  • Work on ASIC design and implementation workflows.

  • Collaborate with physical design, verification, and semiconductor engineering teams.

  • Analyze timing, power, and area (PPA) requirements.

  • Debug design issues and resolve functional and performance-related problems.

  • Perform logic synthesis and support timing closure activities.

  • Review design specifications and prepare technical documentation.

  • Participate in design reviews and continuous improvement initiatives.

Required Skills & Qualifications

  • 2–8 years of experience in VLSI Design or Semiconductor Engineering.

  • Strong programming knowledge of Verilog and SystemVerilog.

  • Experience with RTL design and digital logic design.

  • Understanding of ASIC and SoC design methodologies.

  • Knowledge of synthesis, simulation, and verification processes.

  • Familiarity with timing analysis and optimization.

  • Understanding of CMOS technology and semiconductor fundamentals.

  • Experience with EDA tools such as Synopsys, Cadence, or Siemens EDA.

  • Strong analytical, debugging, and problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, VLSI, or a related field.

  • Experience with FPGA prototyping and ASIC implementation.

  • Knowledge of UVM-based verification methodologies.

  • Familiarity with Static Timing Analysis (STA).

  • Understanding of low-power design techniques.

  • Experience with Python, Tcl, or Perl scripting.

  • Knowledge of physical design, floorplanning, placement, and routing.

Salary & Benefits

  • Annual Salary: $95,000 – $165,000.

  • Competitive compensation based on skills and experience.

  • 100% remote work opportunity.

  • Flexible working arrangements.

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance.

  • Paid time off and holidays.

  • Retirement savings benefits, where applicable.

  • Professional development and career growth opportunities.

Work Location

United States – Fully Remote (Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States).

How to Apply

Interested candidates can submit their updated resume along with contact details and relevant VLSI Design Engineering experience.

Equal Opportunity Employer: We welcome qualified candidates from diverse professional backgrounds and encourage applications from eligible candidates across the United States.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/edgeq-technologies-private-limited-vlsi-design-engineer

Why Mozilla? Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years.

Why Mozilla ? Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people. The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms. About the OS Integration team: The OS Integration team ensures Firefox works well with the host operating system and environment. We’re a distributed team with expertise in Windows, macOS, and Linux-based operating systems. Our responsibilities include developing fixes and improvements for Firefox related to Windows, macOS, and Linux environments. This might include integration with a new OS feature or fixing an OS-specific user interface bug. Other responsibilities include native crash reporting, OS abstraction layers, sandboxing, hardening, updater, and enterprise DLP support. About the role: As a member of the OS Integration team, you’ll develop fixes, improvements, and new features for Firefox. In many cases work may be cross-platform or have a cross-platform component. This role will include maintenance and development of the installer and updater of Firefox. You’ll contribute to the team through code review and discussion. What you’ll do: Improve the quality of Firefox and other Mozilla products by debugging and fixing software defects, improving the browsing experience for hundreds of millions of users. Contribute to new features and improvements. Break down tasks and work with others to deliver solutions. Collaborate with experienced software engineers. Perform code reviews and provide technical direction. Work with a geographically-distributed development team. Interact with teams throughout the organization. What you’ll bring: 5+ years of overall software engineering experience Strong knowledge of C and C++ Experience with desktop application development on Windows, macOS, or Linux with C++. Categories: Developer, Scientific Software Engineer, Software Engineer, Data Processing Engineer, HPC Engineer

OverviewLynker is seeking a highly skilled Software Engineer to support the NOAA/NWS Office of Modeling and Development by managing, developing, and optimizing the meteorological data decoder systems.

Overview Lynker is seeking a highly skilled Software Engineer to support the NOAA/NWS Office of Modeling and Development by managing, developing, and optimizing the meteorological data decoder systems. This role focuses on the critical pipeline that converts diverse, native-format meteorological observations into standardized formats required for downstream numerical weather prediction (NWP) systems. Responsibilities Duties of the Scientific Software Engineer will include the following: Technical Operations & R&D Develop, maintain, and optimize C and Fortran programs used to decode raw meteorological bulletins. Translate non-standard native data formats into BUFR and JEDI IODA netcdf by engineering specialized decoder logic Ensure uninterrupted, efficient data flow by managing input and output streams for ingest data queues, descriptor lists, and temporary BUFR message storage. Systems & Data Integration Monitor and troubleshoot operational data ingestion across major meteorological data servers, including LDM, DBNet, GTS, and WIS2. Ensure decoded data tanks are optimized for rapid assimilation into the NCEP NWP system, supporting the generation of thousands of daily weather products. Manage and maintain the software repositories pertaining to legacy and operational decoder processing. Coordination & Reporting Liaise with upstream data originators and downstream NCO Operations users to seamlessly integrate new observational data types into the BUFR pipeline. Report on software task progress, system performance metrics, and project risks to the Lead Scientist and Federal oversight managers. Participate in the Modernization of Observation Infrastructure project (GEODE) to transition legacy decoder frameworks to modern architectures. Qualifications The Scientist Software Engineer selected for this role should meet the following qualifications: Advanced skills and knowledge of Fortran and C programming languages specifically tailored for data parsing and processing. Deep understanding of BUFR (Binary Universal Form for the Representation of meteorological data), including table-driven descriptors and binary extraction logic. Experience working in a UNIX/Linux environment with advanced shell scripting languages. Demonstrated knowledge of meteorological data servers and distribution networks (LDM, DBNet, GTS, WIS2). Skills and knowledge of High-Performance Computing (HPC) file systems and job schedulers (e.g., WCOSS environment, MPI, Slurm, LSF). Knowledge of modern software development practices and version control software, particularly Git/GitHub/Gitflow. Ability to perform complex, mission-critical debugging in a fast-paced, operational environment. Additional desirable experiences and skills include: Knowledge of global Data Assimilation (DA) systems and observation networks. Experience transitioning legacy meteorological codebases into Cloud environments. Background in atmospheric physics or earth system modeling. About Lynker Lynker is a growing, employee owned business, specializing in professional, scientific and technical services. Our continually expanding team combines scientific expertise with mature, results-driven processes and tools to achieve technically sound, cost effective solutions in hydrology/water sciences, geospatial analysis, information technology, resource management, conservation, and management and business process improvement. We focus on putting the right people in the right place to be effective. And having the right people is critical for success. Our streamlined organization enables and empowers our talented professionals to tackle our customers' scientific and technical priorities – creatively and effectively. Lynker offers a team-oriented work environment, and the opportunity to work in a culture of exceptionally skilled professionals who embrace sound science and creative solutions. Lynker's benefits include the following: Comprehensive healthcare for the employee at no monthly cost Healthcare benefit covers medical, prescription drug, dental, and vision Personal Time Off (PTO) Policy plus paid holidays Highly competitive compensation plan regularly calibrated against industry and location benchmarks 401(k) retirement plan with company-matching Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) – we're all company owners! Flexible spending accounts Employee assistance program (EAP) Short- and long-term disability insurance Life and accident insurance Tuition assistance/Training/Workforce improvement reimbursement per year Spot bonuses for exceptional performance Annual Employee Recognition Awards with bonuses Employee Referral Program Free centralized, self-directed Learning Manage

Who we areAbout StripeStripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses.

Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. About the team The Developer Productivity organization works to make Stripe the most productive place of an engineer’s career. The Code Review team builds the tools and processes that help Stripe engineers review and ship code safely and efficiently. We treat engineers’ attention as a valuable resource, building tools that help them understand changes and focus on the decisions that need human judgment. Our goal is to build an AI review agent that outperforms human review at preventing problems after changes merge, while helping developers move quickly. We are also moving code review from GitHub to Orbit Diffs, Stripe ’s own review interface, and enabling Stripe ’s migration from legacy source control infrastructure to new systems, including infrastructure built at Stripe . What you’ll do As a Staff Software Engineer, you will take ownership of problems across the code review domain, set technical direction, and build alignment across Stripe . You will combine technical leadership with hands-on engineering to build the systems that determine which changes can be approved by agents and when human judgment is needed. Your decisions will influence both the pace and safety of changes across Stripe . You will work across user interfaces, backend services, source control integrations, and agent harnesses. Our team works primarily in Go, Ruby, and TypeScript, and you will use the technologies each problem requires. As AI capabilities evolve, you will experiment with new approaches and turn them into reliable, maintainable tools for developers. Responsibilities Set technical direction for code review, build alignment across Stripe , and mentor engineers as you lead complex projects from problem definition through delivery and adoption Build and improve agent harnesses that enable review agents to exercise judgment and safely approve pull requests Develop evaluations that compare agent and human review decisions, assess the safety of merged changes and the impact on developer velocity, and guide improvements to approval decisions Evaluate and apply advances in AI and agent orchestration to accelerate engineering delivery across Stripe while maintaining review quality, maintainability, reliability, and change safety Build and maintain Orbit Diffs and the surrounding code review tools, helping engineers understand changes and focus their attention where their judgment is most valuable Improve code ownership, intelligent reviewer assignment, stacked pull request workflows, and controls for change management Support Stripe ’s migration to new source control infrastructure by adapting code review workflows and integrations Partner with security, compliance, infrastructure, reliability, and language and runtime teams to improve how software changes are evaluated and approved across Stripe Who you are We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. About Life360

Life360’s mission is to keep people close to the ones they love. Our category-leading mobile app, Tile tracking devices, and Pet GPS tracker empower members to protect the people, pets, and things they care about most with a range of services, including location sharing, safe driver reports, and crash detection with emergency dispatch. Life360 serves approximately 107.7 million monthly active users (MAU), as of September 30, 2026, across more than 180 countries.  

Life360 delivers peace of mind and enhances everyday family life with seamless coordination for all the moments that matter, big and small. By continuing to innovate and deliver for our customers, we have become a household name and the must-have mobile-based membership for families (and those friends who are basically family).

Life360 has more than 500 (and growing!) remote-first employees. For more information, please visit life360.com.

Life360 is a Remote First company, which means a remote work environment will be the primary experience for all employees. All positions, unless otherwise specified, can be performed remotely (within the US and Canada) regardless of any specified location above. 

We are AI Native

We are building an AI native company where AI is an integral part of how we build and operate. AI tool usage during interviews varies by role. You may be asked to demonstrate proficiency with AI tools, discuss how you leverage AI, or complete interview exercises without AI assistance. Your Recruiter will provide clear guidance as you move through the interview process.

Undisclosed use of AI not previously discussed with or approved by your Recruiter may impact your candidacy.

About The Team

This role sits on the Verticals team within Life360 — the group building the next frontier of meaningful connection beyond the core family circle. This role's initial focus is Aging in Place: helping aging parents stay safely independent while giving the families around them real peace of mind. Over time, this role may flex to support other emerging verticals — Things (Tile, connected trackers) or Pets — as priorities shift, so we're looking for someone who wants to help define the pattern for new member segments, not just ship one feature set.

We are a product-minded, AI-Native engineering team. That means AI isn't just a tool we use — it's how we work. We've redesigned our team workflows around AI, treating it as a first-class collaborator at every stage: ideation, coding, testing, review, and iteration. We ship faster and go deeper because of it, and we're looking for someone who wants to help define what that looks like at scale.

About the Job

Life360 is hiring an AI Native Senior Software Engineer — a senior engineer who doesn't just use AI tools, but thinks natively in them. You'll be central to how the Verticals team builds products.

You'll design and build features that serve one of our most important and fastest-growing member segments: aging parents who want to stay safely connected with, and independent from, the families who care about them. As priorities change, you may also apply these same patterns to Things (connected trackers) or Pets.

You will take full ownership of what you build from the first line of code through production, on-call, and the member impact it has. You obsess over the humans on the other end of the product, not just the ticket.

Full-stack experience is required for this role — you should be comfortable moving between backend services and the mobile surfaces that expose them. Our stack spans Spring Boot microservices, Java, Kafka, and Kafka Streams on the backend, a modern cloud-native platform on AWS, and native iOS (Swift) and Android (Kotlin) apps on the client side.

In your first year, success looks like having shipped end-to-end features serving the Aging in Place member segment and establishing at least one AI-native workflow the broader team adopts.

DescriptionMEDvidi is an AI-powered mental healthcare clinic setting a new standard for safe, effective, and scalable psychiatric care in the United States.

Description MEDvidi is an AI-powered mental healthcare clinic setting a new standard for safe, effective, and scalable psychiatric care in the United States. We combine licensed providers with proprietary AI tools to deliver consistent, outcomes-driven treatment for conditions like ADHD, anxiety, depression, and more. MEDvidi ’s technology automates charting, follow-ups, and treatment planning, freeing providers to focus on patient care while improving efficiency and clinical quality. As a Senior Product Designer on our Patient Journey team, you’ll own the patient-facing flows that turn first-time visitors into patients who start and stay in treatment. Your design decisions show up directly in our conversion and retention numbers, not just in the mockups. You’ll be the dedicated designer for the Patient Journey squad, partnering daily with a product manager, frontend and backend engineers, QA, and a data analyst, and reporting to our Director of Product. You own patient-facing flows end to end, from early prototype through validation to a shipped, measurable result in a HIPAA-regulated, AI-first environment where both speed and clarity matter. Responsibilities Own patient-facing conversion flows end to end, from framing the problem through prototyping, validation, and shipped design. Design flows that clearly communicate MEDvidi ’s care model and move patients toward the next step, anticipating their real questions and objections. Partner closely with product and engineering to break “too hard / too long” down into shippable tests that launch in weeks. Dig into product analytics and user research yourself to tie every design decision to a concrete metric: conversion, activation, or retention. Use AI tools to prototype quickly, iterate with your PM, and validate ideas against real users before anything goes to build. This role is not for you if You need a detailed brief before starting work. Requirements here are gathered by you, not handed to you, there is no PM or BA writing specs for AI Track. You prefer managing people over hands-on design. This is an IC role with no direct reports; the impact comes from the quality of your own design decisions. You design exclusively in Figma and hand off static specs. Prototyping at MEDvidi happens in code on the real codebase using AI agents, comfort with a code editor is a daily requirement, not a nice-to-have. Requirements Senior-level product design experience (5+ years) with a strong track record of owning user-facing B2C conversion flows. Demonstrable conversion ownership: you can point to a specific flow where you owned a metric, know the before/after numbers, and can explain your own contribution versus seasonality or marketing. Outcome-driven: comfortable pulling your own data (Amplitude, GA, Metabase, or similar) and running or reading research, rather than waiting for hand-offs. Ownership mindset: you break engineering constraints down to the atoms, negotiate scope, and ship meaningful tests fast. AI as a working tool: fluent with at least one prototyping/AI tool (Lovable, v0, Bolt, Cursor, Claude, or similar) and clear-eyed about where AI should and shouldn’t be used. Fluent Russian and solid working English (B2+) Would be a plus Experience with regulated or healthcare/telehealth products (HIPAA, NIST). What we offer High-impact environment: A chance to contribute to a product-driven company in the medical tech space. Growth & compensation: Clear growth opportunities and a competitive compensation package. Remote-first: Fully remote long-term collaboration under a B2B model. Health & wellness: Health insurance after the probation period, plus sports & wellness compensation. Career development: Clear growth opportunities, including personalized English lessons via Preply. Time off: 19 paid vacation days annually, 4 additional wellness days each year, and paid sick leave for the first 5 working days. Culture: Thoughtful gifts for key life events and offline corporate events. Originally posted on Himalayas

Prototyping & Iteration Build interactive prototypes at the appropriate level of fidelity. Use prototypes to communicate concepts and gather stakeholder feedback. Ensure designs are technically feasible and accurately implemented. Handoff & Developer Support Prepare precise design specifications and assets for engineering handoff. Remain available during development to answer design-related questions. Review implementations and provide feedback on design fidelity. Required Experience & Skills Demonstrated professional experience in UX/UI design. Portfolio showing end-to-end product thinking and strong visual craft. Proficiency in Figma, including component creation, auto-layout, prototyping, and design system management. Solid understanding of UX fundamentals, including information architecture, user flows, interaction design, and accessibility best practices. Experience working in cross-functional product teams alongside engineers and product managers. Strong written and spoken English communication skills. Ability to collaborate asynchronously and clearly present design rationale. What Makes You a Strong Fit You take ownership when requirements are incomplete or ambiguous. You ask the right questions, make reasonable assumptions explicit, and keep work moving forward. You maintain a high standard for visual quality while remaining open to feedback. You treat critique as useful input and separate feedback on the work from personal judgment. You communicate proactively across time zones and surface blockers early. You balance speed and craft, knowing when to move quickly and when a design decision requires deeper exploration. You keep collaborators informed without needing to be prompted. What Success Looks Like Digital product interfaces are polished, user-centered, and aligned with established design standards. User flows and interaction patterns are clear and thoughtfully designed. Engineering teams receive clear, accurate specifications and assets. Implemented designs closely match approved designs. Collaboration remains proactive, clear, and effective across product and engineering teams. From there, you may move into focused design work, refining user flows, producing high-fidelity screens, or building new components for the design system. Later in the day, you might hand off a completed specification to the development team, run a quick usability check on a prototype, or review a developer implementation and flag any discrepancies. Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place. We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused engineering team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Engineers work closely with product teams and company leadership, take features from idea to production, and have a direct role in shaping the platform. Engineering at Bask is AI-first and builder-led. We use tools like Cursor and Claude Code throughout development while maintaining high standards for reliability, testing, and software quality. About the Role We're looking for a UX Researcher, Patient & Provider Experience to help Bask Health better understand how patients and healthcare professionals interact with digital healthcare experiences. Bask Health enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses. Our platform connects patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools. As a UX Researcher, Patient & Provider Experience, you'll investigate how people navigate healthcare-related interfaces, complete important tasks, interpret information, and interact with workflows that may involve sensitive or complex information. This is a hands-on research role focused on evaluating patient and provider experiences through user interviews, usability testing, workflow observation, and qualitative analysis. Your research will help product teams identify where users encounter confusion, unnecessary complexity, or barriers to completing tasks. On the patient side, you'll study experiences such as onboarding, intake questionnaires, form completion, account interactions, and the communication of next steps. You'll investigate whether patients understand the information being requested, can navigate multi-step workflows, and know what to expect after completing an action. On the provider side, you'll study relevant clinical interfaces and operational workflows, including how authorized healthcare professionals review information, navigate tasks, and interact with the platform. You'll pay particular attention to how information moves between patient-facing and provider-facing experiences, identifying usability issues that may affect clarity, efficiency, or workflow continuity. You'll work closely with product designers to evaluate prototypes, test interaction patterns, and improve the organization and presentation of information. You'll collaborate with product managers to define research questions and prioritize studies that address important product decisions. You'll partner with engineers to understand technical constraints and ensure findings can be translated into practical improvements. You'll also collaborate with appropriate clinical and operational stakeholders to understand workflow requirements and ensure research activities respect professional responsibilities and healthcare-related boundaries. Because these experiences may involve sensitive information, you'll conduct research with careful attention to participant privacy, informed consent, approved research environments, and appropriate data-handling procedures. You'll evaluate accessibility, comprehension, and the needs of users with different levels of technical familiarity or healthcare knowledge. You'll synthesize research findings into actionable recommendations that help teams improve usability while preserving the accuracy and intent of healthcare-related workflows. We're looking for someone who is curious about how people interact with healthcare software, comfortable researching complex user journeys, and able to translate detailed observations into meaningful product improvements. devto_hiring::how-to-hire-dedicated-web-.title: How to Hire Dedicated Web Developers in India (2026 Guide)
devto_hiring::how-to-hire-dedicated-web-.description:
TL;DR: Hire dedicated web developers in India when you have an ongoing roadmap, a product owner on your side and at least two hours of daily overlap with the team. In 2026, most estimates put rates at $15–25 an hour for juniors, $25–45 for mid-level, $35–65 for seniors and $50–80 for leads, about $2,400–$12,800 a month full-time. The rate is the easy part. What decides success is interviewing the actual engineers, running a paid trial sprint and getting IP ownership in writing.

Our guide to custom web application development cost compared developer rates by region. The next questions are practical ones. Dedicated team, freelancer or fixed-price project? What should the contract say? How do you know a team is good before you commit?

We're a Delhi studio, so we have an obvious interest in the answer. We've also spent 18+ years and 3,000+ projects on these engagements, and we've seen what makes them work and what makes them fail. This guide covers both, including when you shouldn't hire in India at all.

Why companies hire dedicated web developers from India

Three reasons come up again and again.

Talent depth. India's tech industry directly employs about 5.95 million people, according to Nasscom's 2026 Strategic Review. GitHub's Octoverse 2025 counted 21.9 million Indian developers on the platform, with more than 5.2 million joining in 2025 alone, and projects India will have the world's largest developer community by 2030.

Cost. A full-time Indian developer costs well under a comparable US hire. The realistic saving is smaller than the "70%" in vendor ads (we do the maths below), but it still buys more engineering, more testing or a longer runway.

Speed. Most published estimates put the time to fill a senior engineering role in the US or UK at two to four months, before notice periods. A good dedicated team provider already has vetted engineers and can usually start within days or weeks.

Dedicated team vs fixed-price project vs freelancer vs in-house

"Hiring Indian developers" can mean four very different arrangements. Choose the model first, then the vendor.

Freelancer

Best for small, well-defined tasks: a landing page, a plugin, a bug fix. Fast to start and cheap per hour. The risks are continuity (one person, no holiday cover), no built-in code review and IP terms that depend entirely on what you get them to sign.

Fixed-price project

Best when the scope is tight and stable, such as a clearly specified MVP. The vendor carries the delivery risk, but every change becomes a change request and uncertainty gets priced into the quote. Our MVP development guide explains how to scope one. Fixed-scope work at Netling runs through our Build service, where a typical MVP ships in 8–12 weeks.

devto_hiring::the-problem-of-rigid-exper.title: The Problem of Rigid Experience Requirements in AI-Driven Software Engineering and How to Replace Them
devto_hiring::the-problem-of-rigid-exper.description:
The '5+ Years' Paradox: Why Rigid Requirements Are Failing Modern Tech

Scrolling through modern job boards feels less like engineering assessment and more like an exercise in archaeological dating. When a posting demands "5+ years of experience with Technology X" for a framework, API, or runtime that was publicly released only eighteen months prior, it exposes a catastrophic mechanical failure in how organizations filter human capability.

This absurdity stems from a literalist automation loop. Automated Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) operate on rigid string-matching algorithms. When a recruiter drops a lazy, copy-pasted template into the intake portal, the software executes a blunt token check: it searches the resume text for the exact substring paired with a numerical threshold. The system possesses zero semantic awareness. It cannot calculate that the underlying dependency graph, compiler optimization pipeline, and core paradigm of the technology shifted entirely six months after its initial release, making chronological tenure a negative indicator of adaptability.

In the era of AI-assisted software engineering, this timeline-based filtering breaks down entirely at a workflow and cognitive level. Consider the fundamental shift in how code is produced and maintained:

  • Syntax Generation vs. System Decoupling: Historically, software development was bottlenecked by manual typing speed, syntax memorization, and boilerplate scaffolding. AI code assistants now compress those mechanical writing tasks from days to seconds.
  • The Cognitive Cost of Legacy Tenure: Spending five years manually writing boilerplate in an older paradigm trains an engineer's brain around high-friction workarounds that modern AI tools bypass entirely. Raw years spent typing syntax do not translate to architectural foresight; instead, they often leave cognitive scars—deeply ingrained mental models optimized for constraints that no longer exist.

The structural risk of maintaining these arbitrary numerical filters is precise and severe. When a company enforces a chronological gate, it triggers a catastrophic filtering error: it rejects high-agency, rapidly adapting engineers who master novel toolchains through rigorous first-principles debugging, while admitting legacy practitioners whose primary credential is sheer longevity in a stagnant codebase. If a requirement mathematically exceeds the lifespan of the technology itself, the hiring funnel is no longer measuring competence; it is filtering for template compliance and historical inertia.

The Legacy Blueprint: How HR and ATS Systems Codified Arbitrary Timelines

When a job description demands 5+ years of experience with Technology X, it is rarely the result of a calibrated engineering assessment. Instead, it is the downstream artifact of a historical recruitment pipeline designed for mechanical scale rather than technical fidelity. To understand why these arbitrary timelines persist, we have to examine the mechanical failure points of how talent requirements are translated from engineering reality into HR filters.

Decades ago, software engineering hiring scaled beyond the informal networks of engineering leads. To handle the volume, organizations imported industrial recruitment models, treating software development like manufacturing or mechanical trades where physical wear, muscle memory, and tool handling scaled linearly with tenure. In manual software paradigms, writing raw syntax required repetitive physical inputs and long exposure to boilerplate errors. HR departments and early recruiters operationalized this assumption into a simple proxy: time spent inside an IDE equals operational competence. This proxy was codified into rigid boolean filters within legacy Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS).

The mechanical limitation of these ATS platforms is absolute. An ATS does not parse semantic engineering capability, architectural intuition, or first-principles debugging skill; it executes strict string matching and numerical threshold checks. If a candidate's resume contains fewer than sixty months associated with a specific framework or library string, the system drops the application from the queue before a human engineer ever reviews the codebase context. This creates a closed feedback loop: recruiters copy-paste legacy job description templates featuring chronological thresholds because those templates match the database fields required by the ATS query engine.

This automated filter produces a catastrophic failure of logic when applied to modern technology stacks, resulting in the well-known chronological paradox where postings demand more years of experience than the target framework has actually existed. weworkremotely::circleci-senior-software.title: Senior Software Engineer, Query
weworkremotely::circleci-senior-software.description:
Headquarters: Canada (Remote), United States (Remote), United Kingdom (Remote) Mexico City, Mexico - Hybrid

About CircleCI Engineering

CI/CD has been solved. Now it's being reinvented. AI agents don't just run pipelines. They write code, trigger builds, interpret failures, and propose fixes. The interfaces that developers use to understand and trust that work don't exist yet. We're building them.

At CircleCI, our guiding principles aren't posters on a wall. We learn fast: we run experiments, accept failure, and scale what works. We think like the customer: every decision connects back to the developer sitting in front of a failing build at 2 am. We own the outcome: not just our slice of it, but the whole thing. If that's how you already work, you'll fit here.

About the Query Team

Every pipeline, job, and test that runs on CircleCI generates data, and that history is one of our biggest advantages in an agentic software delivery lifecycle. Flaky test detection, test insights, pipeline search, and agents that reason about why a build failed all depend on fast, reliable access to it.

The Query team owns the system that makes this possible. We pull product data out of the transactional services that create it and store it in datastores built for historical and analytical workloads. We serve it through domain-level APIs to CircleCI's product teams and to customers through our public API. Our goal is to make storing data "fire and forget" for every other team, and querying it fast and dependable at a scale that keeps growing.

What You'll Do

  • Build AI-natively. AI is how we work. It's not a productivity layer on top of engineering, but the default starting point for how problems get approached and solved.
  • Shape how we store data at scale. Own and harden our ClickHouse-based storage layer. Design schemas for known and emerging access patterns, and tune ingestion and query performance to support production-scale data.
  • Build the pipelines that move our data. Design and own ingestion from event streams and durable workflows built on Temporal. Data should arrive reliably, stay queryable while it's in transit, and never slow down the critical path of the services that produce it.
  • Serve data to the product and to customers. Evolve our platform into the default path for historical queries. Make getting historical data easy, not a bottleneck. Teams should be able to get what they need quickly and with minimal hand-holding, while Query keeps enough visibility into how the data is used to optimize ingestion and reads across every consumer. Build in the indexing, caching, and tiered storage required to keep it performant.
  • Set technical direction. When the problem is complex or the answer isn't obvious, you lead the design discussion, write up the architecture decision, and make the call. You help decide which data domain we migrate next and how.
  • Champion observability. Use Honeycomb, Datadog, and Rollbar to understand ingestion lag, query latency, and data correctness. For a data platform, operational data drives stability, not just incident response.
  • Keep things moving. You take ambiguous data problems from design to production quickly, and you help the people around you move faster too.

You don't just patch problems, you ask why they happened. You'll fix the immediate issue, then solve the underlying team practice, process, or system that let it through.

What You'll Bring

  • AI-native engineering practices. You use AI tools daily and can speak to what you've built, where they changed your approach, and where they fall short.
  • Hands-on data experience. You've built or owned data-intensive systems such as ingestion pipelines, event-driven architectures, or analytical and time-series datastores. You understand the tradeoffs between transactional and analytical storage, and you've designed schemas and tuned queries for high-volume workloads. Experience with ClickHouse or another columnar database is a strong plus.
  • Backend depth in Go. You're strong in Go, or strong in a comparable language and eager to work in Go: interface design, data modeling, service integration, and concurrency. Familiarity with React and TypeScript is a plus, since you'll occasionally work on the product surfaces that display this data.
  • Distributed systems judgment. You understand delivery guarantees, idempotency, backpressure, and failure recovery. You know when to rely on a framework's reliability guarantees rather than building your own.
  • Technical leadership. You've led the design of complex systems and made tradeoffs deliberately. You leave

Be Part of Building the Future

Dremio is the unified lakehouse platform for self-service analytics and AI, serving hundreds of global enterprises, including Maersk, Amazon, Regeneron, NetApp, and S&P Global. Customers rely on Dremio for cloud, hybrid, and on-prem lakehouses to power their data mesh, data warehouse migration, data virtualization, and unified data access use cases. Based on open source technologies, including Apache Iceberg and Apache Arrow, Dremio provides an open lakehouse architecture enabling the fastest time to insight and platform flexibility at a fraction of the cost.  Learn more at www.dremio.com.

About the role

Dremio's Query Planner & Reflections (QPR) team owns the SQL planner and optimizer — built on Apache Calcite — and the reflections substitution engine that transparently rewrites queries to hit pre-computed materializations instead of raw source data. As a Staff Software Engineer, you'll set technical direction for this system: driving ambiguous, cross-team initiatives, raising the bar through design and code review, and helping other engineers.

What you'll be doing

  • Set architecture and technical direction for the Query Planner and Reflections team spanning next-generation features across OSS, Enterprise, and Cloud editions.

  • Use AI-assisted development tools for code comprehension, debugging, test generation, documentation, and incident analysis, and apply engineering judgment to validate AI-generated code through review, testing, and benchmarking.

weworkremotely::circleci-staff-software-.title: Staff Software Engineer, Delivery Engineering
weworkremotely::circleci-staff-software-.description:
Headquarters: Remote, Canada (EST) OR Remote, US (EST) OR Remote, UK

About CircleCI Engineering

CI/CD has been solved. Now it's being reinvented. AI agents don't just run pipelines. They write code, trigger builds, interpret failures, and propose fixes. The interfaces that developers use to understand and trust that work don't exist yet. We're building them.

At CircleCI, our guiding principles aren't posters on a wall. We learn fast: we run experiments, accept failure, and scale what works. We think like the customer: every decision connects back to the developer sitting in front of a failing build at 2 am. We own the outcome: not just our slice of it, but the whole thing. If that's how you already work, you'll fit here.

About Delivery Engineering

Delivery Engineering enables CircleCI engineers to deliver quickly, confidently, and securely. We provide the tools and resources that make standard patterns and best practices simple to adopt, and we reduce toil.

Our current focus is the agentic software development lifecycle: how changes are found, planned, built, reviewed, merged, and measured as AI agents take on more of the work. We evaluate the harnesses, repository patterns, skills, and agentic tooling available, decide what our teams should standardize on, and build and support the shared tooling other teams depend on.

We're a small, very senior team, and everyone on it shapes where we go. Every improvement we make compounds across the organization.

What You'll Do

  • Build AI-natively. AI is how we work. It's not a productivity layer on top of engineering, but the default starting point for how problems get approached and solved.
  • Shape how CircleCI builds software with agents. Help define the end-to-end agentic SDLC, from identifying a change through planning, execution, pull request, merge, and measuring impact afterward. Evaluate shared tooling and patterns, and help decide what teams standardize on.
  • Start from how our teams actually work. Spend time with engineering teams to understand their workflows and where they get stuck. Use what you learn to drive decisions and direction that teams adopt because the work fits how they operate.
  • Build platforms, not one-offs. Build and support shared tooling that other teams depend on, and own its adoption as much as its delivery. A tool nobody uses isn't done.
  • Measure what matters. Instrument agent usage and outcomes so we know what improves throughput and quality and what just burns tokens. Treat cost, model choice, and reliability as design concerns.
  • Make build-vs-buy calls. Evaluate models, vendors, and open-source tools against our needs, and choose the path that gets engineers the most leverage.
  • Lead through influence. Write the design docs, lead technical discussions across teams, and mentor engineers across the org as they adopt agentic workflows.

What You'll Bring

  • Direct experience driving agentic developer experience efforts. You've driven an initiative that changed how an engineering organization builds software with AI agents. You can speak to what you built, how you measured its impact, how you drove adoption, and what didn't work.
  • Hands-on depth with agentic tooling. You work daily with coding agents, agent harnesses, MCP, and skills or prompt design. You know how to evaluate agent output and reason about model and token economics.
  • A platform mindset. You've built and supported internal platforms or developer tooling that other engineers build on and rely on, and driven their adoption.
  • Backend depth in Go. You've owned production backend services in Go, including API design, data modeling, and service integration.
  • A track record at staff scope. 8+ years of production engineering experience, including technical decisions that spanned multiple teams and accountability for whether they landed.
  • Decision-making grounded in your users. You build direction by listening first. You turn the needs of many teams into clear tradeoffs, document your reasoning, and bring people along.

This role is open to candidates based in Europe or in the Eastern time zone.

Sound like you?

You've stopped waiting for AI to mature and are already building with it, not as a productivity trick, but as a core part of how you think about problems. You care about the engineers using your tools as much as the code behind them. You're drawn to work where the patterns don't exist yet and the best answer requires you to invent it with the people who'll use it. If that's how you already operate, we want to talk.</

Issuing is the front door for Lithic and its customers’ card payments programs. We can be the reason a launch is successful, a customer signs on or an end user takes up a payment card in their day-to-day life.

Get to know us better CodiLime is a software and network engineering industry expert and the first-choice service partner for top global networking hardware providers, software providers and telecoms.

Get to know us better CodiLime is a software and network engineering industry expert and the first-choice service partner for top global networking hardware providers, software providers and telecoms. We create proofs-of-concept, help our clients build new products, nurture existing ones and provide services in production environments. Our clients include both tech startups and big players in various industries and geographic locations (US, Japan, Israel, Europe). While no longer a startup - we have 250+ people on board and have been operating since 2011 we’ve kept our people-oriented culture. Our values are simple: Act to deliver. Disrupt to grow. Team up to win. The project and the team We develop and integrate software for modern networking platforms and router operating systems for leading equipment manufacturers. In this project, you will join a team supporting the release stabilization and integration of a carried-grade network operating system Rather than traditional network configuration, this role operates "under the hood" of the router's operating system—bridging Embedded Linux, build & release engineering, and automated sanity testing on physical lab hardware and virtualized environments. What else you should know: We work using client-supplied hardware, lab environments, and internal tools The project is managed by the client, with active support from a CodiLime manager The client is based in the US, so early evening syncs may occasionally be required Your role As part of the integration and test team, you will be responsible for: Build & Image Deployment: Pulling code workspaces, resolving Git dependencies, compiling the NOS system images (ISO/RPM), and loading/booting them onto physical routers or virtual targets (e.g., XRv9k). System Layer Integration & Debugging: Troubleshooting issues at the intersection of the router OS and the underlying Linux host—including LXC container startup, SELinux security policies, and Yocto build recipes. CI/CD & Sanity Testing: Executing automated test pipelines and regression suites (using FireX and CAFY), analyzing failure logs (distinguishing image boot crashes from test-case issues), and applying minor fixes to test scripts. Release Stabilization: Supporting developers before release milestones by verifying bug fixes on target hardware, reproducing QA-reported issues, and ensuring nightly builds pass sanity checks without blockers. Do we have a match? To succeed in this role, you should meet the following criteria: Linux Proficiency: Comfortable and well-versed in navigating, debugging, and working within a Linux environment. Router Operating Systems: Practical familiarity with Network operating systems (e.g. Sonic, IOS-XR, Junos OS etc). Device Software Lifecycle Management: Hands-on experience with pulling a workspace, building a system image, and loading/running it directly on a router. Version Control: Strong understanding of Git and Git workflows. Solid CS & Scripting Fundamentals: Good grasp of core computer science concepts and basic scripting (e.g., Python/Bash) to navigate test automation workflows. Nice to have (a big plus): eXR Architecture: Familiarity with the modern 64-bit Linux-based eXR variant of NOS (not a blocker if you know classic NOS and Linux well). Embedded Linux & Containers: Experience with the Yocto Project, LXC (Linux Containers), and SELinux. Internal Tooling: Prior exposure to FireX and CAFY test frameworks (we provide full onboarding for these tools). More reasons to join us Flexible working hours and approach to work: fully remotely, in the office or hybrid Professional growth supported by internal training sessions and a training budget Solid onboarding with a hands-on approach to give you an easy start A great atmosphere among professionals who are passionate about their work The ability to change the project you work on Originally posted on Himalayas

Handle edge cases common in Web3 applications, including pending transactions, reorgs, failed RPC calls, wallet disconnects, chain switching, stale balances, and inconsistent indexer data. Security & Correctness Ensure frontend flows are secure by default, especially when users are asked to sign messages, authorize intents, or store session keys locally. Apply best practices for client-side key management, session key storage, permission scoping, signature domain separation, and phishing-resistant UX. Treat frontend correctness as critical infrastructure, especially when user funds or private information are involved.
